title: K Closest Points to Origin
statement: You get a list of points on a plane, each as [x, y], and a number k. Return the k points closest to the origin (0, 0), using straight-line distance. The points may be returned in any order.

example.caption: k = 2. Squared distances are 18, 26, 20, 2 and 4. The two smallest belong to (1,1) and (0,2).

idea.sentence: Keep the k closest points seen so far in a max-heap by distance, so the farthest of them is on top and is the first one to throw out.

jargon.plain: A container where the biggest item is always on top. Here biggest means farthest from the origin.
x*x + y*y. It skips the square root. If a is closer than b, then its squared distance is smaller too, so the order is the same.

watch.inputHint: Two arguments: the points and k, e.g. [[3,3],[5,-1],[-2,4],[1,1],[0,2]], 2

compare.bruteLabel: Scan for the closest point k times (worst case k = n)
compare.optimalLabel: Heap of size k, n log k (worst case k = n)
compare.unit: comparisons, worst case k = n (the heap does better when k is small)

rows.name: Sort by distance
rows.note: Simple, and fine for small inputs.

rows.name: Max-heap of size k
rows.note: Each point costs one push and at most one pop on a heap of at most k + 1 items.

rows.name: Quickselect
rows.note: Partition around a pivot until the first k points are the closest. Not shown here.

fast.takeaway: A heap of size k beats sorting when k is small, and it works on a stream where you never see all points at once.

stages.title: Squared distance
stages.note: For each point compute x*x + y*y. No square root is needed to compare distances.

stages.title: Push
stages.note: Push the point into a max-heap keyed by that distance.

stages.title: Evict the farthest
stages.note: If the heap holds more than k points, pop the top. It is the farthest, so it cannot be in the answer.

stages.title: Collect
stages.note: After the last point the heap holds exactly the k closest. Return them.

edges.title: k equals n
edges.why: Nothing is ever evicted. The heap just collects everything.

edges.title: A point at the origin
edges.why: Its squared distance is 0, the smallest possible. No special case needed.

edges.title: Equal distances
edges.why: Three points tie at distance 1. Any two is a valid answer, so tests must not rely on which.

edges.title: Negative coordinates
edges.why: Squaring removes the sign. (-3,-4) is at 25 and (2,1) at 5.

gotchas.text: The heap must be a max-heap. A min-heap would put the closest point on top, which is the one you want to keep, not evict.
Compare squared distances. Math.sqrt adds nothing and floating point could make two equal distances look different.

Sorting numbers needs a comparator: [10, 9, 100].sort() is lexicographic and gives [10, 100, 9]. Use (a, b) => a - b. Heap order of equal distances is unspecified, so sort the output before comparing in tests.

container/heap needs five methods: Len, Less, Swap, Push and Pop. Make Less return h[i].d > h[j].d for a max-heap, and call heap.Push and heap.Pop rather than the methods. Pop returns any, so assert the type if you use it.

recap.pattern: Heap: k smallest with a max-heap
recap.key: To keep the k smallest, hold them in a max-heap and evict the top whenever the size passes k.
recap.complexity: Time O(n log k). Space O(k).
moves: If size is over k, pop the farthest
Return the points left in the heap
